newsitem.title: USA: Hillsborough Cty, Fla., seeks Bucs bond rehearing.
newsitem.headline: Hillsborough Cty, Fla., seeks Bucs bond rehearing.

text.p: City of Tampa and Hillsborough County will ask a Florida judge to reconsider his ruling that blocked a $204.5 million bond issue for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' new football stadium, the St. Petersburg Times reported Monday.

Circuit Judge Sam Pendino refused Friday to validate the tax-exempt revenue bond issue by the Tampa Sports Authority. He said a lease provision giving the team the first $2 million of annual revenues from non-Bucs events at the stadium made the project one primarily for private gain, and that it would be unconstitutional to use tax-backed bonds for that purpose.

County Attorney Emmeline Acton told the newspaper she would seek a rehearing before Pendino within 10 days. She said she would argue that the "severability" language in the contract with the team specifies that if one part of the deal is deemed unconstitutional, the rest would be unaffected.
She said that although the judge objected to the $2 million annual payment, the rest of the contract, which uses sales taxes to pay debt service on the bonds, would remain valid.
City and county officials met throughout the weekend with Bucs officials in an attempt to salvage the project.

Former Tampa Mayor Bill Poe had sued to block the bond issue on grounds that it would mainly benefit the privately owned team. He said the local governments gave up their right to seek a rehearing when they signed an agreement in December to merge the lawsuit with the bond validation process.
